Subject: Post-call: token economics confirmation + procurement next steps

Hi Alicia —

Thanks again for taking the call this morning. Quick recap and what I need from you to keep the procurement conversation moving: 

Key items we aligned on from the demo/ops discussion:
- Expected steady-state usage: ~1.2M tokens/month (text + embeddings together).
- Bursty windows: up to ~3.5M tokens in peak months.
- Target unit economics: Orchard is aiming for ~US$600 per 1M tokens for production traffic (goal to hit during committed-reserved pricing).
- Risk/limits: Purchasing needs a clear PO threshold for sign-off — looks like the finance team requires vendor quotes for any monthly spend forecast >US$10k.

What we attached: initial-estimate.csv (breakdown by workload + projected tokens) and procurement-thresholds.pdf (suggested purchase/PO bands and typical SOW language we use).

Ask from you:
1) Can you confirm the preferred procurement band: (A) <US$10k/mo (no PO escalation), (B) US$10k–25k/mo (standard PO), or (C) >US$25k/mo (procurement committee)?
2) If B or C, please share the name/email of the purchasing lead who should be on the thread — we can send a tailored quote and draft PO language.
3) Any internal timeline constraints for signing (target month/quarter)?

Next steps from my side:
- I’ll push a formal quote and a one-page SOW that maps to the 1.2M steady-state with options for a committed 12-month band and on-demand overage.
- Laura will line up a Dedicated capacity cost estimate in case you want reserved throughput.

If it helps, we can finalize a simple 3-band commitment today and route it to Purchasing.

Cheers,

Tessa Morgan
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Tessa —

I ran the numbers for a couple of scenarios. High level:
- Committed 12-month, 1.2M tokens/mo baseline: list pricing equivalent ~US$850/1M; with a 12-month commitment and reserved capacity we can offer US$600/1M as Alicia requested, but that requires a minimum committed spend of US$7k/mo (i.e., a three-band structure where Band B starts at $7k).
- On-demand overage: 20% premium on top of committed unit price for overage tokens.
- Peak-handling option (for their projected 3.5M peak): recommend a burst buffer via Dedicated pools and an agreement clause to cap overage exposure.

I drafted two quick quote lines for Tessa to include in the customer-facing one-pager. I also attached a short procurement-thresholds.pdf with recommended PO language for Michael.

I think we can hit Alicia's goal of US$600/1M if we structure a 12-month reserved commit at their stated baseline.

—Laura
